items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: The first year that Armstrong played with Faith, we were together.

ctx.x: For the booking agent. For the group. For the group, really.

Now we are... Peter Ron never was a member of our band. Peter Booker was a member of our band. He played violin. Yeah. But at this time they make this picture. Peter Ron was a member of our band at that time. He never was. Now you're showing the name of your son of the cornet players? Oh yes. What do you mean? Louis Armstrong. Mark Carey. When did you work with Armstrong? Just... never was a member. But he jobbed around with us in Southern Standard Place at times. He was young. He was very young. He hadn't…
St. Sarah in the band, on the band, John?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: And if you had a corner with good ears, like Lewis Armstrong, you could play a third corner.

ctx.x: You had trombone lead early, way back. The trombone would take the lead.

Yeah, yeah, yeah. Would the trombone usually have the lead instead of the trumpet? And the things that we would make, you know, get together. Or you could steal it from the orchestra, you see. You could steal a part like that from the orchestra and make your trombone part. And if you had a corner with good ears, like Lewis Armstrong, you could play a third corner. See? One of the ears, you couldn't lose that boy on the wing.
When you say, when you steal it from the orchestra, what do you mean by that? Well, make your part. You mean make up a new part?
